test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Foundational Full Test - 02
subject: general
question: A thief noticing a policeman from a distance of 500 metres starts running at a speed of 8 km/h. The policeman chased him with a speed of 11 km/h. What is the distance run by the thief before he was caught? (Rounded off to two decimal places, if required)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **time** is constant, **distance** is directly proportional to **speed**.

Speed Ratio (Policeman : Thief) = 11 : 8

Distance Ratio (Policeman : Thief) = 11 : 8

Difference in distance ratio parts = 11 − 8 = 3 units → 500 m

Distance run by thief = (8 ÷ 3) × 500 = 4000 ÷ 3 = 1333.33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1,333.33 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial distance = 500 m, Speed of thief (Vₜ) = 8 km/h, Speed of policeman (Vₚ) = 11 km/h.

**Formula Used:** Relative Speed = Vₚ − Vₜ | Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed | Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62e5ee22ec334ba23d8315cbdeb4a7790c25d9d6780d1185848ca8d7d65178c0.png] 

⇒ Relative Speed = 11 − 8 = 3 km/h

⇒ 3 km/h in m/s = 3 × (5/18) = 5/6 m/s

⇒ Time to catch = Initial distance ÷ Relative Speed = 500 ÷ (5/6) = (500 × 6) ÷ 5 = 600 seconds

⇒ Speed of thief in m/s = 8 × (5/18) = 20/9 m/s

⇒ Distance run by thief = Speed × Time = (20/9) × 600

⇒ Distance = 12000 ÷ 9 = 4000 ÷ 3 = 1333.33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1,333.33 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds (V₁ − V₂).

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by **5/18**. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by **18/5**.

Proportionality in Motion

If time is constant, **Distance₁/Distance₂ = Speed₁/Speed₂**. This is the most efficient way to solve chase problems.</p
